metadata.scenario: A patient calls to cancel tomorrow's physical therapy session because they have a family emergency. They don't want to reschedule yet and will call back next week. Polite but brief.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret speaking. How can I help you today? Hi Margaret, this is Agnes Rodriguez. I hope you're doing well. Hi Agnes! It's great to hear from you. How are you? I'm okay, but I wanted to cancel my physical therapy session scheduled for tomorrow. Of course, I can help with that. May I ask what the reason is? There's a family emergency I need to attend to. I'm so sorry to hear that. I hope everything is alright. Thank you, it’s just a situation I need to handle. No problem at all. I’ll cancel your appointment for tomorrow. I appreciate it. I don’t want to reschedule just yet—I'll call back next week. That sounds good, Agnes. Just let us know when you’re ready, and we’ll find a suitable time. Will do. I just wanted to make sure to keep you informed. Thank you for keeping us updated. Is there anything else I can assist you with today? No, that’s all for now. Alright, Agnes. Take care of yourself and your family. I will, thank you! Talk to you later. You're welcome! Have a good day. Bye! Bye! (after call ends) I’ll note down the cancellation and follow up with Agnes next week to check in. Plus, I should remind her about our companion care services, especially since she’s feeling isolated. It might be helpful. Let me just update the schedule and make sure her file reflects the cancellation. I’ll also flag this in our notes to ensure we follow up with her next week after her family situation settles down.
